WHAT IS MISSING

ADD VERIFIED CONTEXT

Keep these facts

GUIDANCE ONLY

We don’t invent accomplishments. Add every supporting fact below or use the factual no-number draft.

Edit

Managed project deliverables related to finance processes; [verified detail].

OTHER LINE REWRITES

Useful edits, kept with their own source.

These do not map uniquely to the ranked fixes above, so each stays beside the exact line it rewrites.

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“- Was responsible for preparing financial reports and statements”

REWRITE

Prepared financial reports and statements for [stakeholder group], covering [reporting scope]; [measurable result]

Add the reporting audience, scale, and result so the work reads beyond routine preparation.

LINE EDIT 02 · SOURCE LINE

“- Duties included analyzing budget data and forecasting trends”

REWRITE

Analyzed budget data and forecast trends across [budget scope], providing [analysis or recommendation] to [stakeholder group]; [measurable result]

Add the budget size or coverage, the analysis delivered, and what changed after it was used.

LINE EDIT 03 · SOURCE LINE

“- Participated in team efforts for process improvements”

REWRITE

Participated in process-improvement work for [finance process], contributing [specific action]; [measurable result]

Add the process, your contribution, and the resulting change to distinguish participation from a general claim.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

Which finance process did you own at Linton, and where did your responsibility stop?

Why it may help: Your senior title sits beside several bullets using responsible, assisted, and participated, leaving ownership boundaries unclear.

QUESTION 02

How many departments, budgets, entities, or reports did you handle at Linton Financial Services?

Why it may help: The resume mentions financial reporting and cross-department coordination but gives no size indicator.

QUESTION 03

What changed when you supported month-end and year-end closing at Hartley & Co.?

Why it may help: Closing work is named, but the page does not show deadlines, accuracy demands, or the result of your contribution.

QUESTION 04

What process improvement did you participate in at Hartley & Co., and what changed afterward?

Why it may help: The improvement bullet needs the specific process and measurable or observable change.

QUESTION 05

Which departments did you coordinate with, and what finance issue did the collaboration resolve?

Why it may help: The resume mentions different departments without identifying the stakeholders or the problem addressed.

KEEP THESE

The parts already earning trust.
01

Your titles show a steady progression from Finance Intern in 2011 to Senior Finance Analyst in 2018, which makes the career direction immediately recognizable.

02

Financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, closing, and process work recur across multiple roles, giving the resume a coherent finance foundation.

03

The Linton role includes mentorship and project deliverables, useful details for showing responsibilities beyond individual analysis.

ROLE DIRECTION

Where this story reads strongest.

Position yourself around financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, and finance-process coordination. Replace general collaboration language with the reports, budgets, stakeholders, and results you can verify.

BEST FIT NOW

report.biggest_gap_example: "- Was responsible for preparing financial reports and statements" names a recurring task but not the reports' scale, audience, or business result, so your senior-level contribution is difficult to place.
report.first_impression: The progression from Finance Intern to Senior Finance Analyst is easy to follow, and the finance focus stays consistent. The bullets mostly describe duties, so the page gives little sense of the decisions, scale, or results behind seven-plus years of work.
gaps: Senior-level ownership is not defined: managing project deliverables and mentoring are present, but team size, project scope, and decision authority are absent.
Financial work lacks business context: the page does not identify the reports, forecasts, budgets, or stakeholders you supported.
The summary uses broad phrases such as "results-driven" and "dedicated team player" without naming a finance specialty or concrete accomplishment.

report.score_comment_long: The career progression and finance focus are clear. Most bullets describe responsibilities without numbers, stakeholders, systems, or results. Reworking the two recent roles around verified scope and outcomes is the fastest way to raise the read.
report.score_comment_short: Clear finance progression, but most bullets remain responsibility statements without scope or results.
report.score_plain: This resume can get you considered for finance analyst roles, but it may undersell your seniority. Recruiters will need stronger proof of what you changed, influenced, or handled at scale.

Education.fix: No change needed unless it improves role alignment.
Education.working: The finance degree and graduation date are clear and relevant to the target function.

Work Experience.fix: Rewrite the recent-role bullets with [reporting scope], [stakeholder group], [team size], [system], and [measurable result] where applicable.
Work Experience.missing: The section does not show quantified results, portfolio or budget size, systems, decision-making, or clear ownership.
Work Experience.working: Four finance roles show a consistent progression from intern to senior analyst and cover reporting, forecasting, close, projects, and mentoring.

strengths: Your titles show a steady progression from Finance Intern in 2011 to Senior Finance Analyst in 2018, which makes the career direction immediately recognizable.
Financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, closing, and process work recur across multiple roles, giving the resume a coherent finance foundation.
The Linton role includes mentorship and project deliverables, useful details for showing responsibilities beyond individual analysis.
report.summary: Seven-plus years of finance progression culminate in a Senior Finance Analyst role at Linton Financial Services, with reporting, forecasting, project deliverables, and mentorship as the main through-line. The page fits senior analyst or analyst-level finance searches more readily than manager roles because it does not show direct reports, budget size, or final decision authority. Your work spans core finance operations, but nearly every bullet stops at the task. Until the resume names the reports, stakeholders, systems, and results involved, recruiters may read the senior title as broader than the documented work.
